headline: Cyber law draft: Proposed changes could enable DSA-like abuses, warn experts
summary: Journalists, lawyers, and rights activists warn that amendments to the Cyber Security Act could curb free expression and journalism in Bangladesh.
details: At a seminar organized by the Broadcast Journalists Center (BJC), experts warned that provisions on misinformation, defamation, and content blocking in the proposed Cyber Security Act amendments could be abused to silence dissent.
Critics argue that without adequate safeguards, the new changes could mirror the abuses seen under the previous Digital Security Act (DSA), leading to increased self-censorship among journalists.
Information and Broadcasting Adviser Zahed ur Rahman said the draft is not yet finalized and the government will consider the concerns raised by stakeholders.
The Adviser acknowledged that vague definitions and a lack of proper procedures could create scope for abuse, recalling the misuse of similar laws under the previous administration.
The Daily Star Editor and Publisher Mahfuz Anam suggested separating cybercrime laws from laws governing free expression and online platforms to prevent misuse against writers and cartoonists.

Senior Supreme Court lawyer Sara Hossain and other rights activists called for the removal of criminal defamation, arguing that it is often used to suppress criticism of political figures in a democracy.
Concerns were also raised regarding the power to arrest without a warrant and the excessive power to block content or cancel an organization's license.
The BJC recommended against the blanket criminalization of rumors and unverified information, calling for independent judicial review of content-blocking powers.
caption:
Could the new cyber law amendments lead to a return of the DSA era? Experts warn of potential abuses.

At a seminar organized by the Broadcast Journalists Center (BJC), experts warned that provisions on misinformation, defamation, and content blocking in the proposed Cyber Security Act amendments could be abused to silence dissent.

Critics argue that without adequate safeguards, the new changes could mirror the abuses seen under the previous Digital Security Act (DSA), leading to increased self-censorship among journalists.

Information and Broadcasting Adviser Zahed ur Rahman said the draft is not yet finalized and the government will consider the concerns raised by stakeholders.

The Adviser acknowledged that vague definitions and a lack of proper procedures could create scope for abuse, recalling the misuse of similar laws under the previous administration.

The Daily Star Editor and Publisher Mahfuz Anam suggested separating cybercrime laws from laws governing free expression and online platforms to prevent misuse against writers and cartoonists.

Senior Supreme Court lawyer Sara Hossain and other rights activists called for the removal of criminal defamation, arguing that it is often used to suppress criticism of political figures in a democracy.

Concerns were also raised regarding the power to arrest without a warrant and the excessive power to block content or cancel an organization's license.

The BJC recommended against the blanket criminalization of rumors and unverified information, calling for independent judicial review of content-blocking powers.

headline_marked: PM Tarique [[makes Dubai stopover]] on way home from New York
headline: PM Tarique makes Dubai stopover on way home from New York
summary: The Prime Minister arrives in Dubai after attending the 81st UNGA session in New York, where he addressed global peace and the Rohingya crisis.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman arrived at Dubai International Airport at 8:23pm yesterday, accompanied by his wife Zubaida Rahman and his entourage.
The stopover follows a five-day visit to New York for the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA).
During the session, the Prime Minister delivered his maiden address to the General Debate, focusing on global peace, climate change, and the Rohingya crisis.
He also completed a packed schedule of bilateral meetings with world leaders, UN officials, and representatives of international organizations.
He is scheduled to depart Dubai for Dhaka on flight EK582 at 2:00am on September 27.
The Prime Minister is expected to land at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport at 8:40am on the same day.
caption:
PM Tarique Rahman arrives in Dubai for a brief stopover after wrapping up his maiden UNGA address in New York.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman arrived at Dubai International Airport at 8:23pm yesterday, accompanied by his wife Zubaida Rahman and his entourage.

The stopover follows a five-day visit to New York for the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA).

During the session, the Prime Minister delivered his maiden address to the General Debate, focusing on global peace, climate change, and the Rohingya crisis.

He also completed a packed schedule of bilateral meetings with world leaders, UN officials, and representatives of international organizations.

He is scheduled to depart Dubai for Dhaka on flight EK582 at 2:00am on September 27.

The Prime Minister is expected to land at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport at 8:40am on the same day.
